clauses.reason: Executive Order 6539-A of December 27, 1933 states: "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry." That command is an approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, and it has legal effect only through that approval: under section 3(b) the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, and under sections 3(c) and 3(f) violations were restrainable in equity and punishable as misdemeanors. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no other effective date, so the command ended as a prospective operative command on June 14, 1935. No earlier end is shown (see earlier_end_check). The June 16, 1935 expiry is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory treats the five numbered findings as five clauses and its fifth span (1231-1699) also takes in the operative paragraph and the signature line. The findings are recitals; the only operative command is the final sentence beginning "Now, Therefore" that approves the code, characters 1402 to 1676.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6539-A (December 27, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text has an introductory Whereas paragraph (the Secretary of Agriculture's submission of the code with his report, recommendations and findings), a findings paragraph with five numbered findings (application made; notice and opportunity for hearings given; hearings held; compliance with section 3(a), clauses (1) and (2); tendency to effectuate the policy of section 1), and one operative paragraph ending "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Wine Industry." The machine inventory lists the five numbered findings as five clauses and its fifth span (characters 1231 to 1699) also takes in the operative paragraph and the signature line; findings command nothing, so I replaced the inventory with one clause, characters 1402 to 1676, the operative approval sentence (inventory correction recorded). Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; 1,738 characters). APP page check passed: the mirror page record with the held text's sha256 (common-crawl capture) has a heading naming this order's number, the same date and subject, and a text_sha256 equal to the held text's. Identity also agrees with the census register and the WPA 1944 list (page 560, December 27, 1933). The order's own text states no limit on the approval. An approval of a code under section 3 had legal effect only through section 3, and section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the power to approve codes and the provisions enforcing them, so the first end of this command is June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495, held the code provisions in question invalid on both of its grounds; recorded as a validity characterization of section 3 code approvals, not as an end date for this order. It adjudicated the Live Poultry Code provisions and cancelled or withdrew no other approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1933-06-16: date the Act was approved; states the repealed legal effects of a code approval, not an end date
source_notes.reason: Sections 3(a)-(f) state the legal effects of an approved code that section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed: the code's provisions became the standards of fair competition (3(b)), district courts could restrain violations (3(c)), and violations were misdemeanors (3(f)).
